correction_reason: Adversarial review of the KAN-179 trailer helper found three defects that the sequence-2 suite structurally could not see, plus one related false-skip. D1: append_trailer() concatenated the trailer onto the last line whenever the message contained a body, producing 'Ticket: KAN-179Test-Baseline: <sha>'. The guard compares whole stripped lines, so it never saw the trailer and emitted SOURCE_COMMIT_MISSING_BASELINE_TRAILER. Every pre-existing fixture used a SUBJECT-ONLY message, which is exactly the shape that hides this bug. D2: _resolve_baseline() triggered when ANY staged source path was allowed, but the guard requires that every non-test path in a trailer-carrying commit be inside allowed_source_paths; mixing a docs/ or unlisted source file made the helper manufacture a commit that fails SOURCE_PATH_OUTSIDE_MANIFEST. D3: BYPASS_SUBJECT_PREFIXES included Revert/fixup!/squash!/amend!, none of which appear in the guard's is_release_or_gov exemption list, so those commits were silently left untrailered and then rejected. D4: should_skip() treated any line starting with 'Test-Baseline:' anywhere in the message as an existing trailer, so body prose documenting the format silently disabled the hook. The new suite uses the real scripts/test_provenance_guard.py as its oracle and adds body-bearing fixtures, closing the coverage gap that let the earlier 22/22 green result stand.
rationale: TDD baseline for the KAN-179 Test-Baseline trailer helper defects. RED proven: 10 failed, 2 passed against the sequence-2 helper. GREEN target: 12 passed, with the guard as the end-to-end oracle. The tests commit the helper's OWN output verbatim and then run the real guard, so formatting and decision bugs both reach the gate rather than hiding behind a mock.
